Subject: Action plan request — close timeline & MAP (ACME)

Emily —

Thanks again for the convo this morning. From our end we want to avoid repeated cutover slips and make the decision gates explicit so your team has predictability. Based on the blockers you outlined (legal redlines + procurement approval cadence), I sketched a short re-anchor proposal and a companion risk catalog for the MAP.

Can you confirm whether the procurement approval will be on the 9/27 or the 10/4 cycle? That drives whether we keep the original 10/15 go-live or shift to 10/29.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm procurement cycle date this week.
- We send a re-anchored MAP + risk log with mitigations for each blocker.
- If procurement is 10/4, we propose a hard canary window (10/29–11/5) and a fallback plan for a 2-week staging extension.

I attached a first-pass workbook (ACME_MAP_v3.xlsx) and a CSV risk catalog. I’ll also loop in our sales ops lead if we need an exec alignment call.

Thanks —
Priyom Das

pri...@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Priyom —

Thanks for the summary and for pulling the docs together. Quick answers: legal asked for additional IP carveouts (we escalated last night) so our internal legal loop likely pushes approval to the 10/4 procurement run. Procurement confirmed they will include the contract in the 10/4 packet, but they may still request one more round of redlines after that meeting.

I reviewed the MAP spreadsheet; the risk catalog is useful. A couple immediate asks:
- Can you call out which mitigation requires Redwood engineering time (and an estimated hours bucket)? Our SSO integration requires one short session with your infra team for token exchange validation.
- Can you propose an explicit fallback if procurement asks for an extra legal loop post-10/4?

If you can get an updated MAP with engineering-hours and a tightened fallback this week, I’ll share with my procurement and legal partners before 10/4.

—Emily

2) Add an escalation cadence for any legal counter-redlines (who at Redwood signs off on temporary concessions and at what threshold do we require VP approval).

Emily / team —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per our internal alignment I’m sending a compact executive summary and the decision path:

1) Recommended re-anchor (procurement confirmed 10/4):
   - Canary window: 10/29–11/05
   - Production ramp: 11/12 (full feature set)
   - Engineering sessions: 10/18 10:00–11:30 PDT and 10/21 14:00–15:30 PDT (token validation)

2) Risk catalog highlights and mitigations (see attached close-risk-catalog.csv):
   - Legal extra redline: Mitigation = partial go-live (feature gating) + documented temporary concessions policy (manager sign-off only).
   - Procurement hold: Mitigation = priority standby for customer launch seats + limited credit proposal (if >2 week delay).
   - SSO verification: Mitigation = two short engineering sessions + checklist sign-off.

3) Escalation path:
   - Manager level sign-offs for scoped, reversible concessions.
   - VP-level sign-off required for IP/data/indemnity changes -> triggers canary pause.

4) Docs & actions I pushed to shared Drive: MAP_v4, risk catalog, and the exec one-pager. Doc links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/xyz-map-v3

Next steps for your team: confirm procurement 10/4 in writing and approve the engineering windows (10/18 + 10/21). Once confirmed we’ll send a DocuSign for the agreed temporary concession language and open the canary schedule.

If you prefer an exec sync (15–20 minutes) to lock sign-offs, we’re available 9/30 or 10/1.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
